chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Leaving Verne and recording for Continental
summary: After Verne he recorded about 24 numbers for Continental, which had better distribution abroad; they heard the records in Japan in 1962.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: All right. Now we are into 1948, you are already out of Verne. Was there a reason why you got out of Verne?

Well, things like -- he wasn't making a catalog, you know. They using practically every name that was lose in the market and then made a good catalog, but he, they didn't know very well the record industry. Is a very complicated.
Where was he located at his .....
His office was on Madison, between .....
(End cassette 3, side 1)
We did a lot of numbers .....
Yeah .....
"Nanita"
Yeah, "Me dejan Solito" .....
"Me dejan Solito"
"El Bejuco", all of that. All right, how many tunes did you record for Continental?
Could be twenty-four numbers.
Okay, how many did they release?
I think they released every one.
All of them?
Yeah, but the thing is they had distribution in Europe and South America, all over the place. They had a better distribution abroad that they had in the United States.
Oh, my gosh!! So there is probably a lot of Machito's recordings in those countries that we don't even know about.

As a matter of fact, we heard our records in Japan when we was in 1962, and imagine, that was 1948/'49; and when we went to Japan in 1962, they was playing Continental records up there, numbers that we ......
